common_name: Eclipse Coleus (Deep Purple-Burgundy Foliage Splashed Pink and Green)

planting.note: Plant transplants after all frost danger has passed in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in partial shade; Eclipse is an older sun-shy coleus cultivar bearing large, oval, scallop-edged leaves in deep purple-burgundy overlaid with splashes of pink and green.

directions: Plant nursery starts in spring after the last frost in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix in partial shade, giving it some protection from the harshest midday sun in zone 9's intense summers to keep its dark color from bleaching. Eclipse bears large, oval, scallop-edged leaves in deep purple-burgundy richly splashed with pink and green, an older coleus cultivar now grown mainly by specialty growers and collectors after one of its own branches produced a naturally occurring color-break mutation, discovered within a planting of Eclipse in June 2000 and later introduced and patented as Stained Glassworks Molten Lava, a fiery orange-and-maroon reworking of Eclipse's leaf pattern that has since largely eclipsed the parent's commercial availability. Eclipse itself was never patented. Pinch off flower spikes as they appear to redirect the plant's energy into foliage production, and pinch growing tips periodically through the season to encourage a full, dense, well-branched habit.
sources: U.S. Plant Patent PP14426 (Coleus 'Molten Lava', identifies 'Eclipse' as the unpatented parent cultivar)
